Polar regional models |\n237\t\n238\t---\n239\t\n240\t## Scanning Mode Bits\n241\t\n242\tThe scanning mode (octet 73 in GDT) flags grid point ordering:\n243\t\n244\t| Bit | Value | Meaning |\n245\t|-----|-------|---------|\n246\t| Bit 1 (0x80) | 0 | Points scan +i direction (left to right) |\n247\t| Bit 2 (0x40) | 1 | Points scan +j direction (bottom to top) |\n248\t| Bit 3 (0x20) | 0 | Adjacent points in i-direction are consecutive |\n249\t| Bit 4 (0x10) | 0 | All rows have same number of points |\n250\t\n251\t**Scanning mode 64 (01000000₂)** means:\n252\t- West-to-East scanning (+i)\n253\t- South-to-North scanning (+j)  \n254\t- Consecutive points in i-direction\n255\t- Regular grid (all rows same length)\n256\t\n257\t---\n258\t\n259\t## Tools Used\n260\t\n261\t### Irregularities\n299\t\n300\t1. **Lambert Conformal grids do not store last point coordinates** - These must be calculated via inverse projection from grid indices (Ni-1, Nj-1).\n301\t\n302\t2. Extract parameters:\n74\t   - Grid dimensions: Ni, Nj\n75\t   - First point: Lat1, Lon1\n76\t   - Grid spacing: Dx, Dy (in meters)\n77\t   - Projection: Latin1, Latin2, LaD, LoV\n78\t\n79\t2. Determine min/max lat/lon from corners\n84\t\n85\t#### NAM AWIP12 Extent Example\n86\t\n87\t**Stored parameters:**\n88\t```\n89\tNi = 614, Nj = 428\n90\tLat1 = 12.19°N, Lon1 = 226.541°E\n91\tLatin1 = projection equations (see EPSG:9801).\n103\t\n104\t### Using PROJ / pyproj\n105\t\n106\t```python\n107\tfrom pyproj import Transformer, CRS\n108\t\n109\t# Create Lambert Conformal CRS from GRIB +no_defs\"\n118\t)\n119\t\n120\t# Transform from grid to geographic\n121\ttransformer = Transformer.from_crs(crs, \"EPSG:4326\")\n122\t\n123\t# First grid point in meters (relative to origin)\n124\tx1 = 0  # i=0\n125\ty1 = 0  # j=0\n126\tlon1, lat1 = transformer.transform(x1, y1)\n127\t\n128\t# Last grid point in meters\n129\tx2 = (Ni - 1) * Dx\n130\ty2 = (Nj - 1) * Dy\n131\tlon2, lat2 = It's the primary output format for **GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS, NAM**, and similar numerical weather prediction products.\n56\t\n57\tDecoding it means handling multi-section message framing, four grid geometries, parameter tables indexed by discipline/category/number, five data-packing algorithms, and bitmaps for missing-value masking.\n58\t\n59\tThe standard tools (`wgrib2`, `eccodes`) are C programs. If you need decoded GRIB2 values in a Rust project, your options were: shell out, bind through FFI, or give up and parse bytes yourself.\n60\t\n61\t**gribtract is the native Rust alternative.**\n62\t\n63\t## ✨ Features\n64\t\n65\t- 🦀 **Pure Rust core** — no C toolchain or FFI for simple, complex, complex+spatial-differencing, and PNG packing (DRT 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.41); JPEG2000 (5.40) available behind the optional `jpeg2000` feature\n66\t- 🏷️ **Typed output** — every decoded field carries structured metadata: parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n67\t- 🗺️ **Four grid projections** — lat/lon (GDT 3.0), polar stereographic (3.20), Lambert conformal (3.30), Gaussian (3.40)\n68\t- ⚡ **Lazy decode path** — parse headers only, defer grid data; extract single grid points in **O(1)** for DRT=0 fields without decoding the full grid\n69\t- 📈 **Timeseries extractor** — pull per-station forecast series for a list of lat/lon coordinates in one call\n70\t- 🌐 **Byte-range fetching** — `gribtract-fetch` downloads GRIB2 (or slices of it) from NOAA S3, GCS, and NOMADS over HTTP range requests\n71\t- 🐍 **Python bindings** — `gribtract-py` (PyO3) exposes the decoder to Python\n72\t- ✅ **Oracle-gated correctness** — every release is verified against eccodes/wgrib2 over a corpus of real NOAA files; agreement can only ratchet up\n73\t\n74\t## 📦 Crate Layout\n75\t\n76\t```\n77\tgribtract/\n78\t├── crates/\n79\t│   ├── gribtract-core      # 🔩 Section parser, template decoders, unpacking. No I/O.\n80\t│   ├── gribtract           # 📚 High-level API: message iterator, field selection, timeseries\n81\t│   ├── gribtract-cli       # 💻 `gribtract decode|list|dump` command-line tool\n82\t│   ├── gribtract-fetch     # 🌐 HTTP byte-range fetching from S3 / GCS / NOMADS\n83\t│   ├── gribtract-py        # 🐍 Python bindings via PyO3 (excluded from default build)\n84\t│   └── gribtract-testutil  # 🧪 Differential harness: corpus, golden fixtures, diff\n85\t└── xtask                   # 🛠️ Corpus management, reference-decoder runner, bench dashboard\n86\t```\n87\t\n88\t`gribtract-core` is the zero-dependency parsing core. `gribtract` is the crate you depend on for library use. `gribtract-cli` builds the standalone `gribtract` binary.\n89\t\n90\t## 📖 Usage\n91\t\n92\t### Decode all fields from a GRIB2 file\n93\t\n94\t```rust\n95\tuse gribtract::{decode, Field};\n96\t\n97\tlet bytes = std::fs::read(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\")?;\n98\tlet fields: Vec<Field> = gribtract::decode(&bytes)?;\n99\t\n100\tfor field in &fields {\n101\t    println!(\n102\t        \"param={}/{}/{}  level={}  forecast_offset={}h\",\n103\t        field.parameter.discipline,\n104\t        field.parameter.category,\n105\t        field.parameter.number,\n106\t        field.level.value1(),\n107\t        field.forecast_time.offset_seconds() / 3600,\n108\t    );\n109\t}\n110\t```\n111\t\n112\t### Extract a single grid point — O(1), no full decode\n113\t\n114\t```rust\n115\tuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_point_drt0};\n116\t\n117\tlet fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\n118\tfor lf in &fields {\n119\t    if let Some(body) = &lf.section7_raw {\n120\t        let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(40.64, -73.78)?; // JFK\n121\t        if let Some(value) = decode_point_drt0(body, &lf.packing, idx) {\n122\t            println!(\"value at JFK: {value}\");\n123\t        }\n124\t    }\n125\t}\n126\t```\n127\t\n128\t### Extract a forecast timeseries for a list of stations\n129\t\n130\t```rust\n131\tuse gribtract::timeseries::{extract_timeseries, ParameterRecord, Station, TimeseriesRequest};\n132\t\n133\t// 2m temperature (discipline=0, category=0, number=0), height-above-ground level (type=103)\n134\tlet request = TimeseriesRequest {\n135\t    parameter: ParameterRecord { discipline: 0, category: 0, number: 0 },\n136\t    level_type1: 103,\n137\t    stations: vec![\n138\t        Station { id: \"JFK\".into(), lat: 40.64,  lon: -73.78  },\n139\t        Station { id: \"ORD\".into(), lat: 41.979, lon: -87.905 },\n140\t        Station { id: \"LAX\".into(), lat: 33.943, lon: -118.408 },\n141\t    ],\n142\t};\n143\t\n144\tlet fields = gribtract::decode(&bytes)?;\n145\tlet ts = extract_timeseries(&fields, &request);\n146\t\n147\tfor (station, rows) in &ts.stations {\n148\t    println!(\"Station: {station}\");\n149\t    for row in rows {\n150\t        println!(\"  forecast hour {}: {:?}\", row.forecast_hour, row.value);\n151\t    }\n152\t}\n153\t```\n154\t\n155\t### Decode a DRT=3 grid (complex + spatial differencing) — extract many stations\n156\t\n157\tDRT=3 requires a full sequential decode; random access isn't possible. The recommended pattern is **decode once, extract many**:\n158\t\n159\t```rust\n160\tuse gribtract::{decode_lazy, decode_all_drt3};\n161\t\n162\tlet lazy_fields = gribtract::decode_lazy(&bytes)?;\n163\tfor lf in &lazy_fields {\n164\t    if let (Some(body), Some(extra)) = (&lf.section7_raw, &lf.complex_extra) {\n165\t        let n = lf.grid.num_data_points as usize;\n166\t        let grid: Vec<f64> = decode_all_drt3(body, &lf.packing, extra, n)?;\n167\t\n168\t        // Now extract any number of stations by index, O(1) each\n169\t        for (lat, lon) in &station_coords {\n170\t            let idx = lf.grid.nearest_index(*lat, *lon)?;\n171\t            println!(\"value: {}\", grid[idx]);\n172\t        }\n173\t    }\n174\t}\n175\t```\n176\t\n177\t### 🐍 Python\n178\t\n179\t```bash\n180\tpip install maturin\n181\tmaturin develop -p gribtract-py\n182\t```\n183\t\n184\t```python\n185\timport gribtract\n186\t\n187\tfields = gribtract.decode(open(\"hrrr.t00z.wrfsfcf01.grib2\", \"rb\").read())\n188\tfor f in fields:\n189\t    print(f.parameter, f.level, f.forecast_hour)\n190\t```\n191\t\n192\t## 🔬 The Correctness Oracle\n193\t\n194\tgribtract is built **oracle-first**: correctness is defined as agreement with eccodes/wgrib2 over real files, not as passing hand-written unit tests.\n195\t\n196\t```\n197\tgribtract decode  ─┐\n198\t                   ├─→ compare field-by-field + grid values within derived tolerance\n199\teccodes/wgrib2    ─┘\n200\t```\n201\t\n202\tThe differential harness in `gribtract-testutil` runs both decoders over a corpus of real NOAA GRIB2 files (GFS, HRRR, NBM, GEFS) and compares:\n203\t\n204\t- **Metadata exactly** — center, parameter ID, level, forecast time, grid geometry\n205\t- **Grid values within derived tolerance** — computed from the packing template's own scale factors, never an arbitrary epsilon\n206\t\n207\tAny disagreement becomes a permanent regression fixture. The agreement percentage can only increase; there is no mechanism to silently drop a covered template.\n208\t\n209\t```bash\n210\t# Run the differential tests\n211\tcargo test -p gribtract -- differential\n212\t\n213\t# Fetch and verify against the full corpus (requires eccodes installed)\n214\tcargo xtask corpus fetch\n215\tcargo xtask corpus verify\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\t## 📊 Performance Dashboard\n219\t\n220\tA self-contained benchmark dashboard (`dashboard.html`) tracks decode throughput on real NOAA files, fed by `bench-results.json`. Speed numbers are never reported without a corresponding correctness verification run.\n221\t\n222\t```bash\n223\tcargo xtask bench    # run benchmarks, regenerate bench-results.json\n224\tcargo xtask serve    # serve the live dashboard with streaming updates\n225\t```\n226\t\n227\t## 🏗️ Building from Source\n228\t\n229\tRequires **Rust 1.75+**.\n230\t\n231\t```bash\n232\tgit clone https://github.com/jedarden/gribtract\n233\tcd gribtract\n234\tcargo build --release\n235\t```\n236\t\n237\tThe `gribtract-py` extension is excluded from the default workspace build (it needs Python headers for PyO3) — build it explicitly with `maturin develop -p gribtract-py`.\n238\t\n239\t## 💻 CLI Reference\n240\t\n241\t> **⚠️ Not yet implemented** — The CLI commands below are documented for the planned interface, but are not yet functional.
